history.heading: Empires of the region
paragraphs: Present-day Guinea was part of the Ghana, Mali and Songhai empires; Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire, came from the upper Niger region of Guinea. In the 18th century the Fula established the Islamic state of Futa Jallon in the highlands.
In the late 19th century Samori Touré built the Wassoulou Empire and resisted French conquest until his capture in 1898.

history.heading: French colony and independence
paragraphs: Guinea became a French colony and part of French West Africa. In the 1958 referendum on Charles de Gaulle's French Community, Guinea, led by Ahmed Sékou Touré, was the only colony to vote no, declaring independence on 2 October 1958. France withdrew abruptly, taking equipment and records.

Sékou Touré ruled as a socialist dictator until 1984; thousands of political prisoners died in Camp Boiro. Lansana Conté then ruled until 2008. Alpha Condé, elected in 2010 as Guinea's first democratically elected president, was overthrown in 2021 by Colonel Mamady Doumbouya after changing the constitution to seek a third term.

culture.heading: Peoples and music
paragraphs: The main groups are the Fula (Peul), Malinke and Susu. French is the official language. About 85 percent of people are Muslim.

Guinea has a rich musical tradition of griots, and the Bembeya Jazz National and Les Ballets Africains became internationally famous. Djembe drumming is central to Malinke culture. Rice is the staple food, often served with sauces of cassava leaves or peanuts.

politics.heading: Military transition
paragraphs: Since the 2021 coup, Guinea has been ruled by a military government led by General Mamady Doumbouya. A new constitution was approved by referendum in September 2025, allowing members of the junta to stand for election, and Doumbouya was elected president in December 2025. Opposition activity and protests have been restricted.

economy.heading: Bauxite and iron
paragraphs: Guinea holds the world's largest bauxite reserves and is a leading exporter, mainly to China. The giant Simandou iron ore project, one of the world's richest deposits, began exports in 2025. Gold and diamonds are also mined, and the country has great hydropower potential.
Despite this wealth, most people depend on subsistence farming and poverty is widespread. The currency is the Guinean franc.
